story.outroBody.en: Everything you just saw — and everything we didn't show you — is open to explore. Filter by year, metric, or threshold and see what you find.
story.outroBody.zh: 你刚才看到的一切——以及我们没有展示的一切——都可以自由探索。按年份、指标或阈值筛选，看看你能发现什么。

steps.hook-1.title.en: What a normal year feels like

steps.hook-1.body.en: Every day of the year has a 'normal' in Shanghai. The band stretches from the typical coldest nights (its bottom edge) up to the typical hottest afternoons (its top); the line traces the typical daily high. Muggy Augusts, damp Januaries — the city's rhythm.
steps.hook-1.body.zh: 在上海，一年中的每一天都有自己的“正常值”。色带从典型的最冷夜晚（下缘）一直延伸到典型的最热午后（上缘）；曲线描出典型的每日最高温。闷热的八月、湿冷的一月——这就是这座城市的节奏。

steps.hook-2.body.en: But some days blow straight past normal. Each dot is a day among the most extreme 1% for its date — red above, blue below. The ringed dots carry stories: tap one and see what the newspapers said.
steps.hook-2.body.zh: 但有些日子会直接冲破“正常”。每个圆点都是同期最极端的1%的一天——红色偏热，蓝色偏冷。带圆圈的点背后有故事：点一下，看看当时报纸怎么说。

steps.heat-1.body.en: Zoom into June through September. The hottest days on record cluster stubbornly toward recent years — this is not a smooth spread across four decades.
steps.heat-1.body.zh: 把视线聚焦到6月至9月。有记录以来最热的日子顽固地聚集在近几年——这绝不是四十多年间的均匀分布。

steps.heat-2.body.en: August 3rd, 2024: 38.6°C in the shade, at the peak of a heatwave that pushed the city to its highest alert level. Days like this used to be generational; now they arrive in batches.
steps.heat-2.body.zh: 2024年8月3日：阴凉处38.6°C，正值一场令全市拉响最高级别高温预警的热浪顶峰。这样的日子曾经几十年一遇，如今却成批出现。

steps.heat-3.body.en: Switch to 'feels like' — heat plus Shanghai's humidity — and the picture worsens. July 17th, 1988 remains the record: a feels-like of 46.6°C. The recent years crowd right behind it.
steps.heat-3.body.zh: 切换到“体感温度”——高温叠加上海的湿度——情况更糟。1988年7月17日仍是纪录：体感46.6°C。而近几年正紧随其后。

steps.cold-1.body.en: Now deep winter, January through March. Shanghai cold is its own animal — humid, unheated indoors south of the Huai River line, seeping into everything.
steps.cold-1.body.zh: 现在看隆冬，1月至3月。上海的冷有它自己的性格——潮湿、地处集中供暖线以南的室内寒意，无孔不入。

steps.cold-2.body.en: January 24th, 2016: −8.5°C, feels like −17.5°C. The city's pipes — never built for this — froze and burst across entire districts. Plumbers worked around the clock for a week. Everyone who lived here then remembers.
steps.cold-2.body.zh: 2016年1月24日：−8.5°C，体感−17.5°C。这座城市的水管从未为此设计——整片城区水管冻裂。水管工连续一周昼夜抢修。经历过的人都记得那个冬天。

steps.cold-3.title.en: But the deep cold is fading

steps.cold-3.body.en: The coldest day ever recorded here is January 31st, 1980 — feels like −17.7°C. Look at where the blue dots sit: mostly the 1980s and 90s. The 2016 freeze made headlines precisely because it had become rare.
steps.cold-3.body.zh: 有记录以来最冷的一天是1980年1月31日——体感−17.7°C。看看蓝点的分布：大多在八九十年代。2016年那场寒潮之所以上头条，恰恰因为它已经变得罕见。

steps.rain-1.body.en: Now the water. Each row is a year, each cell a month's total rain. See the dark stripe down June? That's the meiyu — the plum rains — arriving on schedule for 45 straight years.
steps.rain-1.body.zh: 现在看降水。每一行是一年，每一格是一个月的总雨量。看到六月那条深色条纹了吗？那就是梅雨——45年来年年如约而至。

steps.rain-2.body.en: The smoothed line says yearly totals swing hard — the 12 days in June 1999 that dumped 510mm sit next to bone-dry stretches. The heaviest single day in the record: June 30, 1983, with 169.5mm. Three of the ten biggest multi-day soaks happened since 2021.
steps.rain-2.body.zh: 平滑曲线显示年度雨量波动剧烈——1999年6月那12天倾泻了510毫米，紧挨着的却是滴水不下的旱段。纪录中最猛的一天：1983年6月30日，169.5毫米。十大连续暴雨中有三次发生在2021年之后。

steps.rain-3.body.en: Every summer spike in this gust record has a name. The tallest — 109 km/h on July 25, 2021 — is Typhoon In-Fa, which made landfall near Shanghai twice in one weekend. In 2024, Bebinca became the strongest typhoon to hit the city directly since 1949.
steps.rain-3.body.zh: 这张阵风记录里每一根夏季尖峰都有名字。最高的那根——2021年7月25日，109公里/小时——是台风“烟花”，一个周末内两次在上海附近登陆。2024年，“贝碧嘉”成为1949年以来正面袭击上海的最强台风。

steps.aqi-1.body.en: If you lived here in the mid-2010s you remember checking the air before opening a window. The heatmap doesn't forget either: dark winters in 2014 and 2015, when the typical day's PM2.5 index sat at 116 on the US scale — 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', a level China's own standard files under a milder category. Same air, different color depending on whose app you checked. (All values here use the US index.)
steps.aqi-1.body.zh: 如果你在2010年代中期住在这里，你一定记得开窗前先看空气质量。这张热力图也没有忘记：2014、2015年那些深色的冬天，PM2.5指数按美标通常在116——“对敏感人群不健康”，而按中国标准，同样的空气会被归入更温和的等级。同样的空气，不同的App显示不同的颜色。（本图数值均采用美标指数。）

steps.aqi-2.body.en: Watch the rows lighten. The typical day's PM2.5 index fell from 116 in 2014 to 77 in 2025; days over 100 dropped from 227 a year to 87. Still far from pristine — but this is one claim the data settles clearly: Shanghai's air is better than it was a decade ago.
steps.aqi-2.body.zh: 看着一行行颜色变浅。PM2.5指数中位数从2014年的116降到2025年的77；超过100的天数从每年227天降到87天。离真正干净还很远——但这一点数据说得很清楚：上海的空气比十年前好了。

steps.interplay-1.body.en: One dot per day since 2014: temperature across, PM2.5 up, colored by season. The lines trace each season's typical air at each temperature. The pattern isn't one cloud — it's four different seasons behaving four different ways.
steps.interplay-1.body.zh: 2014年以来的每一天都是一个点：横轴是气温，纵轴是PM2.5，颜色代表季节。曲线描出每个季节在不同气温下的典型空气。这不是一团乱点——是四个季节四种脾气。

steps.interplay-2.body.en: Isolate winter and the story sharpens: the coldest days carry the dirtiest air, as northern heating smoke and still air settle over the delta. Shanghai's worst-air days and its coldest days travel together — a pairing summer never matches.
steps.interplay-2.body.zh: 只看冬天，故事就清晰了：最冷的日子往往空气最脏——北方取暖的烟尘加上静稳天气沉积在长三角上空。上海空气最差的日子和最冷的日子结伴而行——夏天从来没有这种组合。

steps.wrap-1.body.en: One year, forty-five times over. The band is where Shanghai's weather is supposed to live; the dots are where it escaped — the heat waves, the frozen pipes, the typhoons and the smog you just met. Now take the controls yourself.
steps.wrap-1.body.zh: 同样的一年，重复了四十五次。色带是上海天气“应该在”的位置；圆点是它逃逸的时刻——你刚刚读到的热浪、冻裂的水管、台风与雾霾。现在，轮到你亲自操作了。
